messages.text: I’ll trace the project settings view, the code that decides whether a project path is available, and existing path-edit flows and tests. I’ll keep this read-only and send the parent a concise report with file and line references.

The screenshot’s “Add” and “Remove” controls match the new-session project picker. Its missing-directory check is asynchronous and only annotates the saved entry; I’m checking whether the separate Settings editor can change that repository path today, and whether any test already covers recovery.
Investigation report delivered to the parent. No files changed.

I’ll follow the Remove action from its asynchronous dashboard result through the controller’s config write and the UI’s refreshed config/state. I’ll focus on whether a missing directory changes removal behavior or leaves the displayed project list stale.

I found no filesystem-existence validation in the remove path or config schema. The refusal gate is based on sessions that still need the bundle; separately, a successful disk removal appears to return no updated config to the dashboard, which may explain a project remaining visible. I’m sending the references and distinction to the parent.

Read-only findings delivered to the parent. Removal has no missing-directory check; its refusal gate is session usage. I also found a separate stale-config path that can leave a successfully removed project visible. No files changed.

I’ll keep the change within `mj-cli` removal completion plumbing and a focused regression test. First I’m checking the working tree and the existing `ConfigLoaded`/create completion patterns so the fix carries the controller’s returned config through the same async update flow.

The remove implementation bypasses the daemon: the CLI calls the controller helper directly, while config snapshots are intentionally owned by the daemon runtime feed. There’s a daemon create-project action but no remove-project action. Fixing this correctly appears to require a daemon API/action addition beyond the assigned `mj-cli` ownership, so I’m handing back that decision with the supporting references before editing.

No edits made. I found that removal runs directly in the CLI, bypassing the daemon’s config mutation coordinator, while the runtime feed is the authoritative config owner. A proper fix appears to need a new daemon remove-project action; I sent the parent the references and asked whether to expand scope.

I’ll extend only the existing `mj-tui` regression to attempt Remove after the missing-path warning, then run that focused test. If it emits the expected action, I’ll report that and investigate an isolated real removal path separately without changing product code.

The Remove click assertion is in place. The first focused test invocation started but stopped before compiling because Cargo has no package named `mj-tui`; I’m checking the workspace package name and will rerun the exact test with that package.

The extended TUI regression passes: clicking Remove on the unavailable project emits `RemoveBundle { bundle_id: "missingpath" }`. I’m keeping this test-only change and now checking the actual isolated removal behavior, especially whether the modal displays a refusal/failure notice as the parent flagged.

The focused `brokk-mj-tui` test passes. I’m building the workspace `mj` binary with `mbx` so I can exercise the saved-project removal in a named isolated instance; the first invocation had to fetch the workspace’s uncached crates, so this build is taking longer than usual.

Status: `mbx test -p brokk-mj-tui a_saved_project_with_a_missing_directory_is_marked_unavailable` passed, including the new click assertion: the unavailable row still emits `RemoveBundle { bundle_id: "missingpath" }`. The user’s quoted message matches the existing static “directory does not exist” detail text. The isolated `mj` binary build is still compiling; I haven’t edited product code.

The new modal-refusal test failed for the intended viewport constraint: the refusal is visible inside the modal, but the long repository detail (“does not exist”) is clipped below it. I’ll assert the unavailable row marker instead, then rerun only this failing test.

The expanded test caught a weak assertion, not a product failure: successful removal correctly leaves “Removed project missingpath.” in the global notice, so checking that the whole render lacks `missingpath` is wrong. I’m narrowing it to the project row/details and the simulated error.

Both focused TUI regressions now pass. The missing-directory picker still emits Remove; the added cases verify the refusal survives inside a short modal, async failure is visible, and a retry/success clears the old result. I’m attempting the isolated binary repro with a local bare target, since this container has no Podman or Docker; `mbx run` is recompiling the binary.

The click-path test and the modal-refusal test pass after correcting two test assumptions (the completion notice still names the deleted project; selecting another row requires keyboard navigation when the short viewport hides it). The isolated binary repro is at 528/553 build steps; configuration uses a missing local directory and the host’s bare target.

The requested focused tests are complete: both pass, including the new unavailable-path refusal rendering at a short viewport. I also ran `cargo fmt -p brokk-mj-tui -- --check` successfully. The separate isolated binary attempt is still compiling `mj-controller`; I’ll report its result or blocker once it finishes.

The focused UI checks are green and formatting is clean. The isolated `mbx run` has reached compilation of `mj-controller` but that crate is taking several minutes on a cold target; I’m continuing because the requested real removal check can exercise the daemon polling path.

The real isolated click reproduced a different failure than the static missing-directory detail: Remove wrote the config (the project is now absent), then failed while hiding its catalog entry with `database writer is not available for operation hide_catalog_project`. The modal now shows that exact error. I’m capturing the isolated state and cleaning up the named test instance.

The actual isolated Remove attempt returned `Could not remove project: database writer is not available for operation hide_catalog_project`. The project row disappeared afterward, so I’m checking the isolated config and shutting down the probe to confirm the partial state cleanly.

Handed the test results and isolated repro to the parent. Focused TUI tests and formatting passed. The real Remove attempt removed the bundle from config but reported `database writer is not available for operation hide_catalog_project`. No product edits or commit from me.

I’ll trace the existing CreateProject/config-mutation path and the current removal completion flow, then add the daemon action and focused RPC regression within the ownership you set. I’ll first identify the precise files I need to touch and avoid the TUI-owned files.

The first-pass ownership surface is `mj-client/src/daemon.rs`, `mj-controller/src/daemon/actions.rs` (plus the nearby controller config mutation helper if required), and `mj-cli/src/dashboard/io/spawn.rs`. I’ll keep all edits there and add the daemon RPC integration regression in the existing controller-side test harness unless it requires changes to a shared test owner.

I’m adding one controller integration test in `mj-controller/src/daemon/tests.rs` because it needs the live daemon RPC/server fixture and isolated database writer. Planned edits are now: `mj-client/src/daemon.rs`, `mj-controller/src/daemon/{actions.rs,state.rs,tests.rs}`, `mj-cli/src/dashboard/io/spawn.rs`, plus the protocol transcript/version fixture if the required bump changes it. I’ll report any additional file before touching it.

The RPC now performs removal through the daemon, updates the controller’s installed config while holding `config_mutation`, publishes a runtime revision, and the CLI awaits only the daemon’s `Result<()>`. The protocol is bumped to 64, with a frozen transcript entry. I’m running the isolated RPC regression; the config/catalog failure ordering is still under parent review, so I haven’t changed that existing helper.

The focused `brokk-mj-controller` test is still compiling the controller test binary; there’s no compiler diagnostic or test result yet. While it builds, I’m keeping the validation scope limited to this RPC regression and the focused client/CLI checks it may require.

The isolated RPC regression passed, including the new partial-failure case: with the database writer stopped, removal fails and the saved config entry remains; with the writer restored, the daemon RPC removes it from config and catalog and publishes the new runtime config. I’m checking the new protocol transcript and then the CLI crate compile path.

The protocol transcript check is relinking the large controller test binary and hasn’t emitted diagnostics; the earlier RPC test binary built and passed. I’ll let this focused check finish, then run formatting and a CLI compile check.

Implementation and focused checks are complete. The daemon removal RPC, config/catalog ordering, runtime-feed publication, and CLI request path are in place; both controller regressions passed, the CLI binary check and workspace format check passed. No full suite or commit was run.

Implemented the daemon-owned removal flow and handed the diff and focused validation results to the parent. The isolated RPC regression and protocol transcript test passed; the CLI check, formatting check, and diff check passed. No commit or full suite was run.
